recommendation_to_G.recommended_rule: Separate supported package API/versioning status from operated-service status. Require an SLO for a concrete owned service/workload boundary. Permit a library package to be covered_by only through a typed, source-bound relation to all actual consumer service SLOs and the exact property those SLIs measure; keep semantic correctness/admissibility evidence separate from availability/latency.
recommendation_to_G.why: public_stable/public_experimental/operational_control labels describe API or governance classes but do not independently prove deployment, traffic, service ownership, or outcome coverage. Current mirror statuses, files, alerts, and runbook references do not prove the whole operational property.
recommendation_to_G.source_bound_existing_slot: architecture/packages/common.toml already declares slo_runbook.status=covered_by_dependents. The current package validator only requires the slot to be nonempty; current operability release gate only accepts present|exception and does not resolve the coverage relation. Reuse this source slot as a prototype anchor, not as an accepted coverage claim.
recommendation_to_G.smallest_missing_capability: One typed covered_by relation consumed by the existing operability release gate: named covering service/SLO owner + complete consumer/workload boundaries + exact metric producer/selector and runbook links + a generic negative test proving a new/unmapped consumer or removed producer fails closed. No new threshold is needed to validate the relationship.

Divergence: runtime predictive-calibration POST exists and emits method-tagged telemetry, but the runtime SLO alert selectors filter method=GET; the current checker does not examine this route-to-selector gap. Separately, non-5xx response success cannot establish security-control correctness.
